You plan to migrate a MySQL database to the managed Cloud SQL service for Google Cloud. Compute Engine virtual machine instances will connect to this Cloud SQL instance, and you do not want to whitelist the instances’ IP addresses for Cloud SQL access.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Enable private IP for the Cloud SQL instance.
Whitelist a project to access Cloud SQL, and add Compute Engine instances in the whitelisted project.
Create a role in Cloud SQL that allows access to the database from external instances, and assign the Compute Engine instances to that role.
Create a CloudSQL instance on one project. Create Compute engine instances in a different project. Create a VPN between these two projects to allow internal access to CloudSQL.

questions.explanation:
Enable private IP for the Cloud SQL instance and configure private services access for its VPC network. Compute Engine instances on that private network can reach the Cloud SQL instance without using public-IP authorized networks, which are the mechanism that requires IP whitelisting.

**Learn more:** [Connect from Compute Engine — Cloud SQL for MySQL](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sql/docs/mysql/connect-compute-engine) · [Learn about using private IP — Cloud SQL for MySQL](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sql/docs/mysql/private-ip)

questions.domain: Integrating applications with Google Cloud services
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your team has developed an application hosted on a GKE cluster. You need to connect the application to a REST service deployed in two GKE clusters across two different regions. How should you configure the connection and health checks? (Choose two.)

options.text: Use Cloud Service Mesh with sidecar proxies to connect the application to the REST service.
Use Cloud Service Mesh with proxyless gRPC to connect the application to the REST service.
Configure the REST service's firewall to allow health checks originating from the GKE service’s IP ranges.
Configure the REST service's firewall to allow health checks originating from the GKE control plane’s IP ranges.
Configure the REST service's firewall to allow health checks originating from the GKE check probe’s IP ranges.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Service Mesh with sidecar proxies supports service-to-service routing and load balancing across multiple regions for HTTP/REST workloads. Proxyless Cloud Service Mesh is specifically a gRPC client deployment model. Firewall rules must allow the health-check probe source IP ranges to reach the REST-service backends so that their health can be evaluated.

**Learn more:** [Cloud Service Mesh load balancing](https://docs.cloud.google.com/service-mesh/v1.25/docs/service-routing/load-balancing) · [Cloud Service Mesh with proxyless gRPC services overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/service-mesh/docs/service-routing/proxyless-overview)

questions.domain: Designing scalable, available, and reliable cloud-native applications
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are a SaaS provider deploying dedicated blogging software for customers in your Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) cluster. You want to configure a secure multi-tenant platform so that every customer can access only their own blog and cannot affect other customers’ workloads. What should you do?

options.text: Enable Application-layer Secrets on the GKE cluster to protect the cluster.
Deploy a namespace per tenant and use Network Policies in each blog deployment.
Use GKE Audit Logging to identify malicious containers and delete them on discovery.
Build a custom image of the blogging software and use Binary Authorization to prevent untrusted image deployments.

questions.explanation:
GKE’s SaaS multi-tenancy guidance recommends organizing each customer application instance in its own namespace so namespace-scoped controls can enforce isolation. Network Policies restrict Pod and Service communication, preventing workloads in one tenant namespace from reaching those in another tenant namespace.

**Learn more:** [Cluster multi-tenancy | Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE)](https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/multitenancy-overview) · [Control communication between Pods and Services using network policies | GKE](https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/network-policy)

questions.domain: Deploying applications
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to containerize a web application to be hosted on Google Cloud behind a global load balancer using SSL certificates. You do not have time to build authentication at the application level, and you want to offload SSL encryption and management from the application. You want to configure the architecture with managed services where possible. What should you do?

options.text: Host the application on Google Kubernetes Engine, and deploy an NGINX Ingress Controller to handle authentication.
Host the application on Google Kubernetes Engine, and deploy cert-manager to manage SSL certificates.
Host the application on Compute Engine, and configure Cloud Endpoints for your application.
Host the application on Google Kubernetes Engine, and use Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) with Cloud Load Balancing and Google-managed certificates.

questions.explanation:
Google Kubernetes Engine provides managed hosting for the containerized application. Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) can protect applications served through Cloud Load Balancing by performing authentication and authorization before requests reach the backend. A global HTTPS load balancer can use Google-managed certificates, offloading TLS certificate provisioning and renewal and terminating HTTPS at the load balancer.

**Learn more:** [Setting up an external Application Load Balancer with IAP](https://cloud.google.com/iap/docs/load-balancer-howto) · [Identity-Aware Proxy overview](https://cloud.google.com/iap/docs/concepts-overview)

questions.domain: Integrating applications with Google Cloud services
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are building a new ecommerce application that uses Cloud Functions. You want to expose your application’s APIs to public users while maintaining a high level of security. You must ensure that only authorized users can access the APIs and that all API traffic is encrypted and safeguarded against unauthorized access. You want the most scalable and secure approach. What should you do?

options.text: Deploy your Cloud Functions behind Cloud Load Balancing, and use Cloud Armor to protect your APIs from distributed denial of service (DDoS) attacks.
Deploy your Cloud Functions with Security Command Center enabled, and use IAM to manage access to your APIs.
Deploy your Cloud Functions behind an Apigee proxy and use Apigee’s authentication and authorization features to secure your APIs.
Deploy your Cloud Functions behind a Cloud API Gateway proxy. Create and use an API key to authorize users to access your APIs.

questions.explanation:
Apigee provides a scalable API proxy layer for securing and managing APIs, including granular security controls and authentication and authorization policies. Its OAuth 2.0 capabilities can generate and validate access tokens for protected APIs. API keys alone are not recommended as the only protection for sensitive API calls because they are included in requests and are less secure than other credentials.

**Learn more:** [What is Apigee?](https://docs.cloud.google.com/apigee/docs/api-platform/get-started/what-apigee) · [Introduction to OAuth 2.0 — Apigee](https://docs.cloud.google.com/apigee/docs/api-platform/security/oauth/oauth-introduction)

questions.domain: Building and testing applications
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an application running in App Engine that is instrumented with Stackdriver Trace. The `/product-details` request returns details about four known, unique products at `/sku-details`, as shown below. You want to decrease the time required for the request to finish.  
  
What should you do?  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783706331233-gmnxta7c.jpg)

options.text: Increase the size of the instance class.
Change the Persistent Disk type to SSD.
Change /product-details to perform the requests in parallel.
Store the /sku-details information in a database, and replace the webservice call with a database query.

questions.explanation:
The four independent `/sku-details` web-service calls are on the request’s sequential latency path, so their durations accumulate. Performing those calls in parallel overlaps their network and service-processing time, reducing overall `/product-details` latency to approximately the longest individual call plus overhead. App Engine supports concurrent request handling.

**Learn more:** [How requests are handled | App Engine standard environment](https://cloud.google.com/appengine/docs/standard/how-requests-are-handled)

questions.question:
You have two tables in an ANSI-SQL-compliant database with identical columns that need to be quickly combined into one table, with duplicate rows removed from the result set.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Use the JOIN operator in SQL to combine the tables.
Use nested WITH statements to combine the tables.
Use the UNION operator in SQL to combine the tables.
Use the UNION ALL operator in SQL to combine the tables.

questions.explanation:
The SQL `UNION` operator combines the results of compatible queries into one result set and excludes duplicate rows. `UNION ALL` instead retains duplicates.\
\
**Learn more:** [Set Operators - UNION (Transact-SQL)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/t-sql/language-elements/set-operators-union-transact-sql?view=sql-server-ver17)

questions.question:
You have two tables in an ANSI-SQL-compliant database with identical columns that need to be quickly combined into one table, with duplicate rows removed from the result set.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Smoke tests
Stackdriver uptime checks
Cloud Load Balancing - heath checks
Managed instance group - heath checks

questions.explanation:
Cloud Monitoring uptime checks periodically send HTTP(S) requests to a public application endpoint and can be paired with an alerting policy that sends notifications when the endpoint fails to respond. This monitors availability through the same externally accessible path used by users.

**Learn more:** [Get notified if your app stops responding](https://docs.cloud.google.com/monitoring/monitoring-uptime) · [Create public uptime checks](https://docs.cloud.google.com/monitoring/uptime-checks?hl=en)

questions.domain: Integrating applications with Google Cloud services
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are building a new application. You want it to run only when a particular file in your Cloud Storage bucket is updated. Because the trigger could change, the process must accommodate different trigger types. You also want a straightforward configuration so multiple team members can modify the triggers later. What should you do?

options.text: Configure Cloud Storage events to be sent to Pub/Sub, and use Pub/Sub events to trigger a Cloud Build job that executes your application.
Create an Eventarc trigger that monitors your Cloud Storage bucket for a specific filename, and set the target as Cloud Run.
Configure a Cloud Function that executes your application and is triggered when an object is updated in Cloud Storage.
Configure a Firebase function that executes your application and is triggered when an object is updated in Cloud Storage.

questions.explanation:
Eventarc provides centrally managed event triggers that filter and route Google Cloud events to a Cloud Run service. Its trigger configuration separates the event source and filtering criteria from the application target, which supports adapting trigger types and maintaining them collaboratively without adding an unnecessary Pub/Sub-to-Cloud-Build pipeline.

**Learn more:** [Route Cloud Storage events to Cloud Run](https://cloud.google.com/eventarc/standard/docs/run/route-trigger-cloud-storage) · [Create triggers with Eventarc for Cloud Run](https://cloud.google.com/run/docs/triggering/trigger-with-events)

questions.domain: Integrating applications with Google Cloud services
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Cloud Run service that must connect to a Cloud SQL instance located in a different project. You granted the Cloud Run service account the Cloud SQL Client IAM role on the project hosting Cloud SQL. However, the connection test fails. You want to resolve the connection failure while following Google-recommended practices. What should you do?

options.text: Add the cloudsql.instances.connect IAM permission to the Cloud Run service account.
Request additional API quota for Cloud SQL Auth Proxy,
Enable the Cloud SQL Admin API in both projects.
Migrate the Cloud SQL instance into the same project as the Cloud Run service.

questions.explanation:
For a cross-project Cloud Run-to-Cloud SQL connection, the Cloud Run service account needs the Cloud SQL Client role on the project that contains the Cloud SQL instance, and the Cloud SQL Admin API must be enabled in both projects. The Cloud SQL Client role already includes the connection permission, so separately adding that permission is unnecessary.

**Learn more:** [Connect from Cloud Run](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sql/docs/mysql/connect-run)

questions.domain: Integrating applications with Google Cloud services
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your team is developing a serverless web application on Cloud Run. The application must access images stored in a private Cloud Storage bucket. You want to grant the application Identity and Access Management (IAM) permission to access the bucket images while securing the services according to Google-recommended best practices. What should you do?

options.text: Enforce signed URLs for the desired bucket. Grant the Storage Object Viewer IAM role on the bucket to the Compute Engine default service account.
Enforce public access prevention for the desired bucket. Grant the Storage Object Viewer IAM role on the bucket to the Compute Engine default service account.

Enforce signed URLs for the desired bucket. Create and update the Cloud Run service to use a user-managed service account. Grant the Storage Object Viewer IAM role on the bucket to the service account.

Enforce public access prevention for the desired bucket. Create and update the Cloud Run service to use a user-managed service account. Grant the Storage Object Viewer IAM role on the bucket to the service account.

questions.explanation:
A Cloud Run service should use a dedicated user-managed service account with the minimum permissions needed for its work. Granting that service account the Storage Object Viewer role on the private bucket authorizes read access to its images. Enforcing public access prevention prevents the bucket and its objects from being accidentally exposed publicly; signed URLs are unnecessary when the Cloud Run workload accesses Cloud Storage through its IAM service identity.

**Learn more:** [Configure service identity for Cloud Run services](https://cloud.google.com/run/docs/configuring/services/service-identity) · [Public access prevention for Cloud Storage](https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/public-access-prevention)

questions.domain: Deploying applications
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are planning a deployment approach for new applications on Google Cloud. As part of the deployment plan, you want to use live traffic to collect performance metrics for both new and existing applications. You must test under the full production load before launch. What should you do?

options.text: Use canary deployment
Use blue/green deployment
Use rolling updates deployment
Use A/B testing with traffic mirroring during deployment

questions.explanation:
Request mirroring copies production requests to a separate backend while the original backend still serves the requests. The mirrored backend can therefore be exercised with full production traffic to evaluate a new version without exposing its responses to users. Google Cloud Load Balancing documents request mirroring as useful for testing a new backend-service version.

**Learn more:** [Set up traffic management for global external Application Load Balancers](https://cloud.google.com/load-balancing/docs/https/setting-up-global-traffic-mgmt)

questions.domain: Integrating applications with Google Cloud services
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your team develops services that run on Google Cloud. You need to build a data-processing service using Cloud Functions. The data that the function must process is sensitive. You need to make sure invocations can occur only from authorized services and follow Google-recommended best practices for securing functions. What should you do?

options.text: Enable Identity-Aware Proxy in your project. Secure function access using its permissions.
Create a service account with the Cloud Functions Viewer role. Use that service account to invoke the function.
Create a service account with the Cloud Functions Invoker role. Use that service account to invoke the function.
Create an OAuth 2.0 client ID for your calling service in the same project as the function you want to secure. Use those credentials to invoke the function.

questions.explanation:
Use a dedicated service account as the calling service’s identity and grant it the Cloud Functions Invoker role (`roles/cloudfunctions.invoker`). That role authorizes invocation of a restricted 1st-generation HTTP function; the calling service authenticates as that service account. The Viewer role provides read-only access and does not authorize invocation, while an OAuth client ID does not itself grant IAM permission to invoke the function.

**Learn more:** [Cloud Functions IAM Roles](https://docs.cloud.google.com/functions/docs/reference/iam/roles) · [Authenticate for invocation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/functions/docs/securing/authenticating)

questions.domain: Designing scalable, available, and reliable cloud-native applications
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are responsible for planning the staged migration of your company’s on-premises application to Google Cloud. The company’s monolithic ecommerce website will be migrated to microservices deployed on Google Cloud in stages. Because most company revenue comes from online sales, minimizing migration risk is important. You need to prioritize features and choose the first functionality to migrate. What should you do?

options.text: Migrate the Product catalog, which has integrations to the frontend and product database.
Migrate Payment processing, which has integrations to the frontend, order database, and third-party payment vendor.
Migrate Order fulfillment, which has integrations to the order database, inventory system, and third-party shipping vendor.
Migrate the Shopping cart, which has integrations to the frontend, cart database, inventory system, and payment processing system.

questions.explanation:
A first migration candidate should be less business-critical and as loosely coupled as possible, so migration mistakes do not disrupt the primary revenue path while the team builds cloud experience. Product catalog has only frontend and product-database integrations among the choices, whereas payment processing directly affects financial transactions, order fulfillment involves inventory and a third-party shipping vendor, and the shopping cart also depends on inventory and payment processing. Google Cloud guidance specifically advises against selecting an ecommerce workload’s main financial-transactions component as a first mover and recommends loosely coupled workloads when dependencies are unavoidable.

**Learn more:** [Migrate to Google Cloud: Assess and discover your workloads](https://docs.cloud.google.com/architecture/migration-to-gcp-assessing-and-discovering-your-workloads)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An analytics system runs queries against a BigQuery dataset. The SQL query runs in batch, passes the contents of a SQL file to the BigQuery CLI, and then redirects the BigQuery CLI output to another process. However, the BigQuery CLI returns a permission error when the queries run.  
  
You want to fix the issue. What should you do?

options.text: Grant the service account BigQuery Data Viewer and BigQuery Job User roles.
Grant the service account BigQuery Data Editor and BigQuery Data Viewer roles.
Create a view in BigQuery from the SQL query and SELECT* from the view in the CLI.
Create a new dataset in BigQuery, and copy the source table to the new dataset Query the new dataset and table from the CLI.

questions.explanation:
BigQuery query execution requires `bigquery.jobs.create` in the project where the job runs and read access to every referenced table or view. The BigQuery Job User role grants query-job creation, and the BigQuery Data Viewer role grants access to query the dataset data.

**Learn more:** [Run a query | BigQuery | Google Cloud Documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/running-queries?hl=en) · [BigQuery IAM roles and permissions | Google Cloud Documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/access-control)

questions.question: HipLocal’s APIs have occasional application failures. They want to gather application information specifically to troubleshoot the problem. What should they do?

options.text: Take frequent snapshots of the virtual machines.
Install the Cloud Logging agent on the virtual machines.
Install the Cloud Monitoring agent on the virtual machines.
Use Cloud Trace to look for performance bottlenecks.

questions.explanation:
Application logs provide the runtime events, errors, and diagnostic details needed to investigate intermittent API failures. Installing the Cloud Logging agent on Compute Engine virtual machines sends those logs to Cloud Logging for centralized analysis. Cloud Monitoring primarily collects metrics, Cloud Trace analyzes request latency, and VM snapshots do not capture ongoing application log data.\
\
**Learn more:** [Troubleshoot the Logging agent](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/agent/logging/troubleshooting)

questions.question: HipLocal’s APIs have occasional application failures. They want to gather application information specifically to troubleshoot the problem. What should they do?

options.text: Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *
Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://*.example.com
Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://fn.example.com
Access-Control-Allow-origin: https://www.example.com

questions.explanation:
`Access-Control-Allow-Origin` authorizes a specific requesting origin for cross-origin browser requests. Setting it to `https://www.example.com` permits clients served from that origin to call the function at `https://fn.example.com`; it neither permits every origin nor incorrectly authorizes the function’s own origin. HTTP header field names are case-insensitive. Google Cloud documents configuring cross-origin access to an HTTP function by setting `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` on its response.

**Learn more:** [Write Cloud Run functions — CORS](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/write-functions)

questions.domain: Building and testing applications
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are developing an application with a microservices architecture that includes Cloud Run, Bigtable, and Pub/Sub. You want to perform testing and debugging as quickly as possible in order to create a minimally viable product at minimal cost. What should you do?

options.text: Use Cloud Shell Editor and Cloud Shell to deploy the application, and test the functionality by using the Google Cloud console in the project.
Use emulators to test the functionality of cloud resources locally, and deploy the code to your Google Cloud project.
Use Cloud Build to create a pipeline, and add the unit testing stage and the manual approval stage. Deploy the code to your Google Cloud project.
Use Cloud Code to develop, deploy, and test microservices resources. Use Cloud Logging to review the resource logs.

questions.explanation: Emulators for Bigtable and Pub/Sub enable local testing and debugging without incurring cloud infrastructure costs, supporting fast iteration during MVP development. Developers can validate microservice logic, data flows, and integrations entirely offline before deploying to GCP. This minimizes early-stage costs while enabling rapid feedback cycles. Cloud Code requires deployment to fully test; Cloud Build adds process overhead unsuitable for rapid MVP iteration.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company requires a database solution to store customer purchase history that meets these requirements:  
  
- Customers can query a purchase immediately after it is submitted.  
- Purchases can be sorted by a variety of fields.  
- Different record formats can be stored simultaneously.  
  
Which storage option meets these requirements?

options.text: Firestore in Native mode
Cloud Storage using an object read
Cloud SQL using a SQL SELECT statement
Firestore in Datastore mode using a global query

questions.explanation:
Firestore in Native mode provides a strongly consistent, document-based database with real-time capabilities. Its flexible document model permits records with different field structures, and its indexes support ordering queries on fields in ascending or descending order. This allows newly submitted purchases to be queried immediately and sorted by the required fields.

**Learn more:** [Choosing between Native mode and Datastore mode](https://docs.cloud.google.com/datastore/docs/firestore-or-datastore) · [Standard edition index overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/firestore/native/docs/standard-index-overview)

questions.domain: Integrating applications with Google Cloud services

options.text: Each developer commits their code to the main branch before each product release, conducts testing, and rolls back if integration issues are detected.
Each group of developers copies the repository, commits their changes to their repository, and merges their code into the main repository before each product release.
Each developer creates a branch for their own work, commits their changes to their branch, and merges their code into the main branch daily.

Each group of developers creates a feature branch from the main branch for their work, commits their changes to their branch, and merges their code into the main branch after the change advisory board approves it.

questions.explanation:
Trunk-based development and continuous integration use short-lived branches and frequent integration into the main branch. Merging daily exposes integration problems early, reduces long-lived branch divergence and merge conflicts, and supports faster software delivery.

**Learn more:** [DevOps capabilities](https://docs.cloud.google.com/architecture/devops) · [Best practices for continuous integration and delivery to Google Kubernetes Engine](https://cloud.google.com/solutions/best-practices-continuous-integration-delivery-kubernetes)

questions.question: Which service should HipLocal use to provide secure, authorized access to its internal apps?

options.text: Cloud VPN
Cloud Armor
Virtual Private Cloud
Cloud Identity-Aware Proxy

questions.explanation:
Cloud Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) enforces authentication and authorization for access to protected applications at the application layer. It supports secure, identity-based access to internal web applications without granting broad network-level access.\
\
**Learn more:** [Identity-Aware Proxy documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/iap/docs) · [Identity-Aware Proxy overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/iap/docs/concepts-overview)

options.text: Set a retention policy on the bucket with a period of 7 years.
Use IAM Conditions to provide access to objects 7 years after the object creation date.
Enable Object Versioning to prevent objects from being accidentally deleted for 7 years after object creation.
Create an object lifecycle policy on the bucket that moves objects from Standard Storage to Archive Storage after 3 years.

Implement a Cloud Function that checks the age of each object in the bucket and moves the objects older than 3 years to a second bucket with the Archive Storage class. Use Cloud Scheduler to trigger the Cloud Function on a daily schedule.

questions.explanation:
A 7-year bucket retention policy prevents objects from being deleted or replaced before they reach seven years of age. An Object Lifecycle Management rule can automatically transition Standard Storage objects to Archive Storage after three years, which is suited to very infrequently accessed data and lowers at-rest storage costs. These controls work together: the retention policy protects the objects for the required period while the lifecycle rule changes their storage class without requiring a separate bucket or scheduled function.

**Learn more:** [Bucket Lock](https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/bucket-lock) · [Object Lifecycle Management](https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/lifecycle)

questions.domain: Integrating applications with Google Cloud services
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An application running in Cloud Run validates bucket names against your organization’s compliance rule. You want the Cloud Run application to receive a notification as soon as possible whenever a new Cloud Storage bucket is created, and to alert the project owner if the bucket name is noncompliant. You must configure the notification according to Google-recommended practices. What should you do?

options.text: Create a log-based metric with an alerting policy that sends a notification using the webhook to the Cloud Run endpoint.
Configure an Eventarc trigger using the storage.buckets.create filter that sends a notification to the Cloud Run endpoint.
Configure a log-based alerting policy using the storage.buckets.create filter in the audit logs that sends a notification to the Cloud Run webhook.
Configure a log-based alerting policy using the storage.buckets.create filter in the audit logs that sends a notification to a Pub/Sub topic that is pushed to the Cloud Run service.

questions.explanation:
Eventarc routes matching Google Cloud events to Cloud Run as HTTP CloudEvents. A Cloud Storage bucket-creation operation can be filtered by the Cloud Audit Logs method name `storage.buckets.create`, allowing the Cloud Run service to validate the new bucket promptly without relying on log-based monitoring alerts or an unnecessary Pub/Sub hop.

**Learn more:** [Route audit log events to Cloud Run](https://docs.cloud.google.com/eventarc/standard/docs/run/route-trigger-cloud-audit-logs) · [Route Cloud Storage events to Cloud Run](https://docs.cloud.google.com/eventarc/standard/docs/run/route-trigger-cloud-storage)

questions.domain: Deploying applications
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are developing a web application using Cloud Run and Cloud Storage. You are alerted to a production issue that must be troubleshot immediately. You need to implement a workaround that requires executing a script on a Git repository. Your corporate laptop is unavailable, but you have your personal computer. You can use your corporate credentials to access the required Git repository and Google Cloud resources. You want to resolve the issue as quickly and efficiently as possible while minimizing additional cost. What should you do?

options.text: Create and launch a workstation with Cloud Workstations on your personal computer. Authenticate and set up API access in the workstation. Clone the Git repository and execute the workaround script. Ensure that the issue has been fixed.

Install VS Code and the extension Cloud Code for VS Code on your personal computer. Check the Cloud Run logs in Cloud Code to confirm the error. Execute the workaround script. Ensure that the issue has been fixed.
Connect to the Google Cloud console and open Cloud Shell on your personal computer. Clone the Git repository and execute the workaround script. Ensure that the issue has been fixed.
Download and install the gcloud CLI on your personal computer. Authenticate and set up API access. Clone the Git repository and execute the workaround script. Ensure that the issue has been fixed.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Shell provides a browser-based, temporary managed environment with the Google Cloud CLI and Git already installed, so it can access Google Cloud resources and clone and run the repository script without installing or configuring tools on the personal computer. Cloud Shell is free for users with a Google Cloud account.

**Learn more:** [How Cloud Shell works](https://docs.cloud.google.com/shell/docs/how-cloud-shell-works) · [Cloud Shell pricing](https://cloud.google.com/shell/pricing)

You are configuring a VM instance for development and must select either SSD or Standard Persistent Disks for the VM. Your team’s cloud architect is currently unavailable to consult. You need to promptly identify the advantages and disadvantages of SSD versus Standard storage. What should you do?

options.text: Use Gemini Cloud Assist, and prompt “What is the difference between SSD and Standard Persistent Disks?”
Request help on internet forums such as Reddit or Stack Overflow.
Review the Google Cloud documentation on Persistent Disks.
Review reference architectures that match your application in the Cloud Architecture Center.

questions.explanation:
Google Cloud’s Persistent Disk documentation directly describes the tradeoffs between disk types: SSD Persistent Disk is intended for lower latency and higher IOPS, while Standard Persistent Disk uses HDD and is economical for workloads dominated by sequential I/O. This authoritative documentation provides the relevant basis for selecting the storage type.

**Learn more:** [Persistent Disk — Compute Engine](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/disks/persistent-disks)

questions.explanation: Cloud Build automates container image construction and registry upload. lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],The current application stores user-state data in one MySQL database. This state data is highly user-specific and strongly depends on how long a user has used the application. The MySQL database makes it difficult to maintain and enhance the schema for different users.  
  
Which storage option should you select?

options.text: Cloud SQL
Cloud Storage
Cloud Spanner
Cloud Datastore/Firestore

questions.explanation:
Cloud Datastore/Firestore is a schemaless NoSQL database, allowing user-state entities or documents to have different properties and property types without requiring a single relational schema migration for all users. This accommodates user-specific state that changes as users progress through an application.

**Learn more:** [Entities, Properties, and Keys | Datastore | Google Cloud Documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/datastore/docs/concepts/entities) · [Data model | Firestore in Native mode | Google Cloud Documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/firestore/native/docs/data-model)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are a developer at a large corporation and manage three GKE clusters. Your team’s developers must regularly switch between clusters on the same workstation. You want to configure secure, individual access to these multiple clusters according to Google-recommended practices. What should you do?

options.text: Ask the developers to use Cloud Shell and run the gcloud container clusters get-credentials command to switch to another cluster.
Ask the developers to open three terminals on their workstation and use the kubectl config set command to configure access to each cluster.
Ask the developers to install the gcloud CLI on their workstation and run the gcloud container clusters get-credentials command to switch to another cluster.
In a text file, define the clusters, users, and contexts. Email the file to the developers and ask them to use the kubectl config set command to add cluster, user, and context details to the file.

questions.explanation:
Install the Google Cloud CLI on each developer’s workstation and use `gcloud container clusters get-credentials` for the target cluster. The command creates or updates the developer’s kubeconfig using that developer’s authenticated Google Cloud identity and changes kubectl’s current context to the selected cluster. This avoids manually distributing credential configuration and supports switching securely among GKE clusters.

**Learn more:** [Install kubectl and configure cluster access](https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/cluster-access-for-kubectl) · [gcloud container clusters get-credentials](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sdk/gcloud/reference/container/clusters/get-credentials)

questions.domain: Deploying applications
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to deploy a new feature to production on Cloud Run. Your company’s SRE team requires gradual deployments to prevent major downtime caused by code-change errors. You want to configure this deployment with minimal effort. What should you do?

options.text: Configure the application’s frontend load balancer to toggle between the new and old revisions.
Configure the application code to send a small percentage of users to the newly deployed revision.

Deploy the feature with “Serve this revision immediately” unchecked, and configure the new revision to serve a small percentage of traffic. Check for errors, and increase traffic to the revision as appropriate.

Deploy the feature with “Serve this revision immediately” checked. Check for errors, roll back to the previous revision, and repeat the process until you have verified that the deployment is bug-free.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Run natively supports gradual rollouts through revision traffic splitting. Deploying without immediately serving the new revision preserves the current revision’s traffic; the new revision can receive a small percentage, be monitored for errors, and have its traffic allocation increased progressively without redeployment.

**Learn more:** [Rollbacks, gradual rollouts, and traffic migration | Cloud Run](https://cloud.google.com/run/docs/rollouts-rollbacks-traffic-migration)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You work for an ecommerce company and are designing a new Orders API that will be exposed through Apigee. In your Apigee organization, you created two new environments named `orders-test` and `orders-prod`. You plan to use distinct URLs, `test.lnk-42.com/api/v1/orders` and `Ink-42.com/api/v1/orders`, for each environment. You need to ensure that each environment uses only its assigned URL. What should you do?

options.text: 1. Attach orders-test and orders-prod to the orders environment group.2. Add each hostname to the appropriate environment.
1. Attach orders-test and orders-prod to the orders environment group.2. Add each hostname to the orders environment group.
1. Attach orders-test to the test environment group, and attach orders-prod to the production environment group.2. Add each hostname to the appropriate environment.
1. Attach orders-test to the test environment group, and attach orders-prod to the production environment group.2. Add each hostname to the appropriate environment group.

questions.explanation:
Apigee defines hostnames on environment groups rather than on individual environments. All environments in the same group share that group’s hostnames, so separating `orders-test` and `orders-prod` into test and production environment groups and assigning each hostname to its respective group ensures each environment is reachable only through its assigned hostname.

**Learn more:** [About environments and environment groups](https://docs.cloud.google.com/apigee/docs/api-platform/fundamentals/environments-overview) · [Working with environment groups](https://docs.cloud.google.com/apigee/docs/api-platform/fundamentals/environmentgroups-working-with?hl=en)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization has recently launched an initiative to replatform its legacy applications onto Google Kubernetes Engine. You must decompose a monolithic application into microservices. Multiple instances need read and write access to a configuration file stored on a shared file system. You want to minimize the management effort for this transition and avoid rewriting the application code. What should you do?

options.text: Create a new Cloud Storage bucket, and mount it via FUSE in the container.
Create a new persistent disk, and mount the volume as a shared PersistentVolume.
Create a new Filestore instance, and mount the volume as an NFS PersistentVolume.
Create a new ConfigMap and volumeMount to store the contents of the configuration file.

questions.explanation:
Filestore provides fully managed NFS storage for GKE and supports `ReadWriteMany` PersistentVolumes, allowing multiple Pods or nodes to concurrently read and write the same shared filesystem. This preserves the application’s existing file-based access pattern without requiring application code changes.

**Learn more:** [About Filestore support for Google Kubernetes Engine](https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/filestore-for-gke) · [Storage for GKE clusters overview](https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/storage-overview)

You are in the final phase of migrating an on-premises data center to Google Cloud. As the deadline rapidly approaches, you discover that a web API is running on a server scheduled for decommissioning. You must recommend an approach to modernize this API as it is migrated to Google Cloud. The modernized web API must satisfy these requirements:  
  
- Autoscales during high-traffic periods at the end of each month  
- Is written in Python 3.x  
- Lets developers rapidly deploy new versions in response to frequent code changes  
  
You want to minimize the cost, effort, and operational overhead of this migration. What should you do?

options.text: Modernize and deploy the code on App Engine flexible environment.
Modernize and deploy the code on App Engine standard environment.
Deploy the modernized application to an n1-standard-1 Compute Engine instance.
Ask the development team to re-write the application to run as a Docker container on Google Kubernetes Engine.

questions.explanation:
App Engine standard environment is a fully managed platform with Python 3 runtimes and automatic scaling, allowing application versions to be deployed without managing virtual machines or Kubernetes clusters. This satisfies the traffic and rapid-release requirements with less operational overhead than VM-based flexible environment, Compute Engine, or GKE deployments.

**Learn more:** [App Engine standard environment overview](https://cloud.google.com/appengine/docs/standard/overview) · [Python 3 Runtime Environment — App Engine standard environment](https://cloud.google.com/appengine/docs/standard/python3/runtime)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have recently joined a new team with a Cloud Spanner database instance running in production. Your manager asks you to optimize the Spanner instance to reduce costs while preserving the database's high reliability and availability. What should you do?

options.text: Use Cloud Logging to check for error logs, and reduce Spanner processing units by small increments until you find the minimum capacity required.
Use Cloud Trace to monitor the requests per sec of incoming requests to Spanner, and reduce Spanner processing units by small increments until you find the minimum capacity required.
Use Cloud Monitoring to monitor the CPU utilization, and reduce Spanner processing units by small increments until you find the minimum capacity required.
Use Snapshot Debugger to check for application errors, and reduce Spanner processing units by small increments until you find the minimum capacity required.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Spanner capacity should be reduced gradually while monitoring CPU utilization in Cloud Monitoring. Adequate CPU headroom is required for the instance to continue serving traffic during failures and to complete critical background work, so CPU utilization is the relevant metric for safely finding the minimum processing-unit capacity.

**Learn more:** [Compute capacity, nodes and processing units — Spanner](https://docs.cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/compute-capacity) · [CPU utilization metrics — Spanner](https://docs.cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/cpu-utilization)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],For this question, refer to the HipLocal case study.  
  
HipLocal's application uses Cloud Client Libraries to interact with Google Cloud. HipLocal needs to set up authentication and authorization in the Cloud Client Libraries to apply least-privileged access for the application. What should they do?

options.text: Create an API key. Use the API key to interact with Google Cloud.
Use the default compute service account to interact with Google Cloud.
Create a service account for the application. Export and deploy the private key for the application. Use the service account to interact with Google Cloud.

Create a service account for the application and for each Google Cloud API used by the application. Export and deploy the private keys used by the application. Use the service account with one Google Cloud API to interact with Google Cloud.

questions.explanation:
A dedicated application service account can be granted only the IAM roles required by the Google Cloud resources and APIs it uses, providing a distinct workload identity with least-privileged authorization. API keys do not provide equivalent IAM-based authorization, and default service accounts are not recommended for least privilege because they can be highly privileged. Google Cloud client libraries use Application Default Credentials with service-account credentials for authentication.

**Learn more:** [Set up ADC for a resource with an attached service account](https://cloud.google.com/docs/authentication/set-up-adc-attached-service-account) · [How Application Default Credentials works](https://cloud.google.com/docs/authentication/application-default-credentials)

questions.domain: Designing scalable, available, and reliable cloud-native applications
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are a developer working for a local concert venue. Customers use your company’s website to buy tickets for events. You need to give customers immediate confirmation when their selected seat has been reserved. How should you design the ticket-ordering process?

options.text: Upload the seat reservation to a Cloud Storage bucket, which triggers an event to the backend service that processes the seat reservation.

Submit the seat reservation in an HTTP POST request to an Application Load Balancer. Configure the Application Load Balancer to distribute the request to the backend service that processes the seat reservation.
Add the seat reservation to a Cloud Tasks queue, which triggers Workflows to process the seat reservation.
Publish the seat reservation to a Pub/Sub topic. Configure the backend service to subscribe to the topic to process the seat reservation.

questions.explanation:
An HTTP POST through an Application Load Balancer routes the customer request to a backend service and keeps the HTTP request-response interaction available for that service to return the completed reservation result. Application Load Balancers distribute HTTP(S) traffic to backends, whereas Cloud Tasks and Pub/Sub are designed for asynchronous processing.

**Learn more:** [Application Load Balancer overview](https://cloud.google.com/load-balancing/docs/application-load-balancer) · [Understand Cloud Tasks](https://cloud.google.com/tasks/docs/dual-overview)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Data is stored in Cloud Storage buckets. Fellow developers report that downloading data from Cloud Storage results in slow API performance.  
  
You want to investigate the issue and provide details to the GCP support team.  
  
Which command should you run?

options.text: gsutil test ג€
gsutil perfdiag ג€
gcloud compute scp example-instance:~/test-data ג€
gcloud services test ג€

questions.explanation:
`gsutil perfdiag` performs Cloud Storage bucket performance diagnostics, including tests relevant to transfer performance, and can save its results to an output file for support analysis. Google Cloud documentation identifies `gsutil perfdiag` as a Cloud Storage diagnostic and lists the bucket and object permissions required to run it.

**Learn more:** [IAM permissions for gsutil commands](https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/access-control/iam-gsutil) · [Optimizing your Cloud Storage performance: Google Cloud Performance Atlas](https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/gcp/optimizing-your-cloud-storage-performance-google-cloud-performance-atlas)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have recently developed an application that will be hosted on Cloud Run. You need to perform a load test. You want to examine the load-test logs second by second to understand your Cloud Run service's response to rapid traffic spikes. You want to minimize effort. How should you analyze the logs?

options.text: Use estimation to extrapolate performance from summary monitoring charts.
Analyze the log data in BigQuery by configuring a BigQuery log sink with the appropriate inclusion filter for your application.
Use Cloud Monitoring’s default log console for analysis.
Analyze the log data in Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL by pushing logs to a Pub/Sub topic. Use Dataflow to process and ingest the logs.

questions.explanation:
A Cloud Logging sink can route only the relevant application log entries, using an inclusion filter, to a BigQuery dataset. BigQuery supports querying the routed log records and their timestamps at the needed fine granularity, without building a Pub/Sub, Dataflow, and Cloud SQL ingestion pipeline.

**Learn more:** [View logs routed to BigQuery](https://docs.cloud.google.com/logging/docs/export/bigquery) · [Route log entries](https://docs.cloud.google.com/logging/docs/routing/overview)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are building a dashboard that aggregates temperature readings from thousands of IoT devices that monitor a city’s ambient temperature. You anticipate substantial viewing traffic, resulting in significant data egress after the dashboard goes live. The dashboard’s temperature-display data does not have to be real-time and can tolerate a few seconds of lag. You decide to deploy Memorystore for Redis as the storage backend. You want to make sure that the dashboard is highly available. How should you configure the service in Memorystore for Redis?

options.text: Update Memorystore for Redis to the latest version.
Configure Memorystore to use read replicas.
Use Private Service Access to enable low-latency network throughput.
Set up Serverless VPC Access to avoid receiving traffic over the internet.

questions.explanation:
Memorystore for Redis read replicas scale read-heavy workloads through a read endpoint and use asynchronous replication, which can result in a few seconds of replica lag. In the Standard Tier, replicas also support high availability through automatic failover if the primary fails.

**Learn more:** [About read replicas | Memorystore for Redis](https://docs.cloud.google.com/memorystore/docs/redis/about-read-replicas) · [High availability for Memorystore for Redis](https://docs.cloud.google.com/memorystore/docs/redis/high-availability-for-memorystore-for-redis)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You must deploy resources from your laptop to Google Cloud with Terraform. Resources in your Google Cloud environment must be created by using a service account. Your Cloud Identity has the Identity and Access Management (IAM) role `roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator` and the required permissions to deploy the resources with Terraform. You want to configure your development environment to deploy the required resources according to Google-recommended best practices. What should you do?

options.text: 1. Download the service account’s key file in JSON format, and store it locally on your laptop.2. Set the GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS environment variable to the path of your downloaded key file.

1. Run the following command from a command line: gcloud config set auth/impersonate_service_account [email protected].2. Set the GOOGLE_OAUTH_ACCESS_TOKEN environment variable to the value that is returned by the gcloud auth print-access-token command.
1. Run the following command from a command line: gcloud auth application-default login.2. In the browser window that opens, authenticate using your personal credentials.

1. Store the service account's key file in JSON format in Hashicorp Vault.2. Integrate Terraform with Vault to retrieve the key file dynamically, and authenticate to Vault using a short-lived access token.

questions.explanation:
Service account impersonation lets a principal with `roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator` obtain short-lived credentials for a service account. Setting `auth/impersonate_service_account` causes the Google Cloud CLI to use short-lived service-account credentials, so the access token supplied to Terraform authenticates Terraform as that service account. This avoids downloading and managing a long-lived service account key.

**Learn more:** [Use service account impersonation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/docs/authentication/use-service-account-impersonation) · [How Application Default Credentials works](https://docs.cloud.google.com/docs/authentication/application-default-credentials)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to configure a Deployment on Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE). You want to add a check to confirm that the containers can connect to the database. If the Pod cannot connect, you want a script in the container to run and perform a graceful shutdown. How should you configure the Deployment?

options.text: Create two jobs: one that checks whether the container can connect to the database, and another that runs the shutdown script if the Pod is failing.

Create the Deployment with a livenessProbe for the container that will fail if the container can't connect to the database. Configure a Prestop lifecycle handler that runs the shutdown script if the container is failing.
Create the Deployment with a PostStart lifecycle handler that checks the service availability. Configure a PreStop lifecycle handler that runs the shutdown script if the container is failing.
Create the Deployment with an initContainer that checks the service availability. Configure a Prestop lifecycle handler that runs the shutdown script if the Pod is failing.

questions.explanation:
A liveness probe can check database connectivity and, after its failure threshold is reached, Kubernetes terminates and restarts the unhealthy container. A `PreStop` lifecycle handler is invoked immediately before termination, including termination caused by a liveness-probe failure, allowing the container’s graceful-shutdown script to run.

**Learn more:** [Liveness, Readiness, and Startup Probes](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/probes/) · [Container Lifecycle Hooks](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/containers/container-lifecycle-hooks/)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your development team uses Cloud Build to promote a Node.js application built on App Engine from its staging environment to production. The application depends on several photo directories stored in a Cloud Storage bucket named `webphotos-staging` in the staging environment. After promotion, these photos must be available in a Cloud Storage bucket named `webphotos-prod` in the production environment. You want to automate the process wherever possible. What should you do?

options.text: Manually copy the photos to webphotos-prod.
Add a startup script in the application's app.yami file to move the photos from webphotos-staging to webphotos-prod.
![](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783707039598-0ujcda6v.png)
![](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783707041993-uyy3k0y7.png)

questions.explanation: Cloud Build orchestrates ordered build steps, including Cloud Storage operations. A gsutil copy step in cloudbuild.yaml before the App Engine promotion step recursively transfers photo directories from webphotos-staging to webphotos-prod, ensuring production content is populated before application promotion. Startup scripts are not suitable for pre-deployment data preparation, and manual copying removes automation.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You recently developed an application that monitors a large number of stock prices. You need to configure Pub/Sub to receive a high volume of messages and update the current stock price in one large in-memory database. A downstream service requires the most up-to-date prices in the in-memory database to perform stock-trading transactions. Each message contains three pieces of information:  
  
- Stock symbol  
- Stock price  
- Timestamp for the update  
  
How should you configure your Pub/Sub subscription?

options.text: Create a pull subscription with exactly-once delivery enabled.
Create a push subscription with both ordering and exactly-once delivery turned off.
Create a push subscription with exactly-once delivery enabled.
Create a pull subscription with both ordering and exactly-once delivery turned off.

questions.explanation:
A pull subscription supports high-throughput, batched, massively parallel consumption. The timestamp allows the in-memory database to accept only a price update newer than the currently stored timestamp for that stock symbol, so duplicate or late messages cannot replace the latest price. Ordering and exactly-once delivery are therefore unnecessary; both add coordination that can increase latency and reduce availability.

**Learn more:** [Choose a subscription type](https://cloud.google.com/pubsub/docs/subscriber) · [Troubleshooting a pull subscription](https://cloud.google.com/pubsub/docs/pull-troubleshooting)

questions.domain: Deploying applications
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an application managed by a managed instance group. When you deploy a new application version, costs must be minimized and the instance count must not increase. You need to ensure that, whenever a new instance is created, deployment proceeds only if that new instance is healthy.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Perform a rolling-action with maxSurge set to 1, maxUnavailable set to 0.
Perform a rolling-action with maxSurge set to 0, maxUnavailable set to 1
Perform a rolling-action with maxHealthy set to 1, maxUnhealthy set to 0.
Perform a rolling-action with maxHealthy set to 0, maxUnhealthy set to 1.

questions.explanation:
A rolling update with `maxSurge` set to 0 prevents the managed instance group from creating instances above its target size, avoiding the added cost of surge capacity. Setting `maxUnavailable` to 1 restricts the update to one unavailable replacement at a time. With health checking enabled, a replacement is not considered available until it reports healthy, so further rollout is held until that instance becomes healthy.

**Learn more:** [Automatically apply VM configuration updates in a MIG](https://docs.cloud.google.com/compute/docs/instance-groups/rolling-out-updates-to-managed-instance-groups)

questions.domain: Deploying applications

options.text: Create a Cloud Storage bucket in each region, and create a Cloud Run service of the payment processing application in each region.
Create a Cloud Storage bucket in each region, and create three Cloud Run services of the payment processing application in the Singapore region.
Create three Cloud Storage buckets in the Asia multi-region, and create three Cloud Run services of the payment processing application in the Singapore region.
Create three Cloud Storage buckets in the Asia multi-region, and create three Cloud Run revisions of the payment processing application in the Singapore region.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Run services reside in a selected region, and customer data associated with a service is stored in that region. Regional Cloud Storage buckets place object data in their chosen region. Deploying a bucket and a Cloud Run service in each transaction country meets country-specific data residency and keeps processing colocated with its data, avoiding cross-region access costs. The Cloud Storage `ASIA` multi-region explicitly excludes Hong Kong and Indonesia, so it cannot satisfy the Jakarta and Hong Kong residency requirements.

**Learn more:** [Cloud Run locations](https://cloud.google.com/run/docs/locations?hl=en) · [Cloud Storage bucket locations](https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/bucket-locations)

You recently deployed a Go application to Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE). The operations team has observed that the application's CPU usage remains high even with low production traffic. They have asked you to optimize the application's CPU resource consumption. You want to identify which Go functions use the greatest amount of CPU. What should you do?

options.text: Deploy a Fluent Bit daemonset on the GKE cluster to log data in Cloud Logging. Analyze the logs to get insights into your application code’s performance.
Create a custom dashboard in Cloud Monitoring to evaluate the CPU performance metrics of your application.
Connect to your GKE nodes using SSH. Run the top command on the shell to extract the CPU utilization of your application.
Modify your Go application to capture profiling data. Analyze the CPU metrics of your application in flame graphs in Profiler.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Profiler supports CPU-time profiling for Go applications running on GKE. Adding the profiling agent to the application collects function-level CPU data, and Profiler flame graphs show each function’s relative CPU consumption, enabling identification of the CPU-intensive functions to optimize.

**Learn more:** [Profiling Go applications](https://docs.cloud.google.com/profiler/docs/profiling-go) · [Flame graphs](https://docs.cloud.google.com/profiler/docs/concepts-flame)

questions.domain: Deploying applications
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are developing a new API that creates requests on an asynchronous messaging service. Different services will consume the requests. You need to expose the API through a gRPC interface while minimizing infrastructure-management overhead. How should you deploy the API?

options.text: Deploy your API to App Engine. Create a Pub/Sub topic, and configure your API to push messages to the topic.
Deploy your API as a Cloud Run service. Create a Pub/Sub topic, and configure your API to push messages to the topic.
Deploy your API to a GKE cluster. Create a Kafka cluster, and configure your API to write messages to the cluster.
Deploy your API on a Compute Engine instance. Create a Kafka cluster, and configure your API to write messages to the cluster.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Run is fully managed and supports gRPC end-to-end, making it appropriate for hosting the API without managing servers or a cluster. Publishing requests to a Pub/Sub topic decouples the API from the services that consume the messages and provides managed asynchronous messaging.

**Learn more:** [Using gRPC | Cloud Run](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/triggering/grpc) · [What is Pub/Sub? | Google Cloud Documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/pubsub/docs/overview)

questions.domain: Designing scalable, available, and reliable cloud-native applications
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company’s product team has a new customer-driven requirement to autoscale its stateless, distributed service running in a Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) cluster. You want a solution that minimizes changes because this feature will go live in two weeks. What should you do?

options.text: Deploy a Vertical Pod Autoscaler, and scale based on the CPU load.
Deploy a Vertical Pod Autoscaler, and scale based on a custom metric.
Deploy a Horizontal Pod Autoscaler, and scale based on the CPU toad.
Deploy a Horizontal Pod Autoscaler, and scale based on a custom metric.

questions.explanation:
A Horizontal Pod Autoscaler increases or decreases the number of Pod replicas for a workload. CPU utilization is a built-in metric, so scaling on CPU requires fewer changes than implementing and exporting a custom metric. A Vertical Pod Autoscaler adjusts per-Pod resource requests instead of scaling the replica count.

**Learn more:** [Horizontal Pod autoscaling | Google Kubernetes Engine](https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/horizontalpodautoscaler) · [Configuring horizontal Pod autoscaling | Google Kubernetes Engine](https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/horizontal-pod-autoscaling)

questions.domain: Building and testing applications
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your team is creating unit tests for Cloud Function code. The code is stored in a Cloud Source Repositories repository. You are responsible for implementing the tests. Only one specific service account has the required permissions to deploy the code to Cloud Functions. You need to ensure the code cannot be deployed until the tests have passed. How should you configure the unit-testing process?

options.text: Configure Cloud Build to deploy the Cloud Function. If the code passes the tests, a deployment approval is sent to you.
Configure Cloud Build to deploy the Cloud Function, using the specific service account as the build agent. Run the unit tests after successful deployment.
Configure Cloud Build to run the unit tests. If the code passes the tests, the developer deploys the Cloud Function.
Configure Cloud Build to run the unit tests, using the specific service account as the build agent. If the code passes the tests, Cloud Build deploys the Cloud Function.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Build runs build steps in sequence, so unit-test steps can be placed before the Cloud Functions deployment step. Configuring the build to use the service account that holds the deployment permissions lets Cloud Build deploy only after the tests complete successfully; a failed test prevents subsequent deployment steps from running.

**Learn more:** [Deploying to Cloud Run functions](https://cloud.google.com/build/docs/deploying-builds/deploy-functions) · [Default Cloud Build service account](https://cloud.google.com/build/docs/cloud-build-service-account)

You are developing an application that shares PDF files containing time-sensitive information with users. The PDF files are stored in Cloud Storage, and you must provide secure access to them.  
  
You have these requirements:  
  
- Users must have access only to files they are permitted to view.  
- Users must be able to request read, write, or delete access to the PDF files for 24 hours.  
  
Not every application user has a Google account. How should you provide access to data objects?

options.text: Configure the application to generate signed URLs with an expiration time of 24 hours. Share the signed URLs with users. Attach the signed URL to the PDF files that users require access to.

Provide users with the Service Account Token Creator IAM role to impersonate the application's service account. Assign the Cloud Storage User IAM role to the application's service account to access the Cloud Storage bucket. Rotate the application's service account key every 24 hours.

Generate a service account that grants access to the POF files. Configure the application to provide users with a download link to the service account's key file. Set an expiration time of 24 hours to the service account Keys. Instruct users to authenticate by using the service account key file.
Assign the Storage Object User IAM role to users that request access to the PDF files. Set an IAM condition on the role to expire after 24 hours.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Storage signed URLs grant time-limited permission for a specific request against a specific object and work for anyone who possesses the URL, including users without Google accounts. The application can authorize each user before issuing a signed URL for the required read, write, or delete operation, with a 24-hour expiration. IAM roles require authenticated principals, while sharing service account key files exposes credentials and is not an appropriate user-access mechanism.

**Learn more:** [Signed URLs | Cloud Storage](https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/access-control/signed-urls) · [Overview of access control | Cloud Storage](https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/access-control)

questions.domain: Building and testing applications
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You work for an organization that operates an ecommerce site. Your application is deployed behind an external Application Load Balancer. You need to test a new product-recommendation algorithm. You plan to use A/B testing to determine, in a randomized manner, the new algorithm’s effect on sales. How should you test this feature?

options.text: Split traffic between versions using weights.
Enable the new recommendation feature flag on a single instance.
Mirror traffic to the new version of your application.
Use HTTP header-based routing.

questions.explanation:
Application Load Balancer listener rules can forward requests to multiple target groups using relative weights. Splitting production requests between target groups running the existing and new versions creates randomized treatment and control populations whose sales outcomes can be compared for an A/B test.

**Learn more:** [Action types for listener rules - Elastic Load Balancing](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/rule-action-types.html)

questions.domain: Deploying applications
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company plans to migrate its on-premises Hadoop environment to the cloud. Rising storage costs and the maintenance burden of data kept in HDFS are major concerns. You also want to make minimal changes to the existing data analytics jobs and architecture.  
  
How should you carry out the migration?

options.text: Migrate your data stored in Hadoop to BigQuery. Change your jobs to source their information from BigQuery instead of the on-premises Hadoop environment.
Create Compute Engine instances with HDD instead of SSD to save costs. Then perform a full migration of your existing environment into the new one in Compute Engine instances.

Create a Cloud Dataproc cluster on Google Cloud Platform, and then migrate your Hadoop environment to the new Cloud Dataproc cluster. Move your HDFS data into larger HDD disks to save on storage costs.

Create a Cloud Dataproc cluster on Google Cloud Platform, and then migrate your Hadoop code objects to the new cluster. Move your data to Cloud Storage and leverage the Cloud Dataproc connector to run jobs on that data.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Dataproc runs Hadoop workloads in a managed service, and its preinstalled Cloud Storage connector enables Hadoop jobs to read and write Cloud Storage directly using HDFS-compatible access. Moving persistent data from HDFS to Cloud Storage reduces HDFS storage administration while retaining the existing Hadoop job model with minimal changes.

**Learn more:** [Dataproc FAQ — Data access and availability](https://cloud.google.com/dataproc/docs/resources/faq) · [Cloud Storage connector — Managed Service for Apache Spark](https://cloud.google.com/managed-spark/docs/concepts/connectors/cloud-storage)

questions.domain: Designing scalable, available, and reliable cloud-native applications
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are building a short-term image-hosting service in which end users worldwide can upload images of up to 20MB, and the images are automatically deleted after 10 days. You need to decide how to store the images while minimizing cost. How should the images be stored?

options.text: Write the image to a Cloud Storage bucket. Create a lifecycle configuration that deletes objects 10 days older than their creation date.
Write the images to Spanner. Configure a row deletion policy on the table that deletes rows 10 days older than their creation date.
Write the images to Firestore. Deploy a Cloud Scheduler-invoked Cloud Run service that queries for documents written 10 days prior to today and deletes them.
Write the images to Bigtable. Configure a garbage collection policy for the column family that deletes cells 10 days older than their creation date.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Storage provides cost-effective object storage for image files and supports Object Lifecycle Management. A bucket lifecycle rule with a `Delete` action and an `age` condition of 10 days automatically deletes objects once they reach that age, without requiring a custom cleanup workload.

**Learn more:** [Object Lifecycle Management | Cloud Storage | Google Cloud Documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/lifecycle)

questions.domain: Designing scalable, available, and reliable cloud-native applications
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company has a BigQuery data mart that supplies analytics information to hundreds of employees. One user wants to run jobs without interrupting important workloads. This user is not concerned about how long these jobs take to run. You want to meet this request while minimizing company cost and the effort required from you.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Ask the user to run the jobs as batch jobs.
Create a separate project for the user to run jobs.
Add the user as a job.user role in the existing project.
Allow the user to run jobs when important workloads are not running.

questions.explanation:
BigQuery batch query jobs have lower priority than interactive jobs and are more likely to remain queued while a project or reservation is using all available compute resources. They are therefore suited to non-time-sensitive work that should yield to important workloads, without creating separate projects or manually coordinating execution times. [Run a query | BigQuery](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/running-queries)

**Learn more:** [Run a query | BigQuery](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/running-queries)

questions.domain: Integrating applications with Google Cloud services
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are building a new ecommerce website for your company. You want customers to get a customized email notification when they submit an order. You need to configure this email service while minimizing deployment effort. What should you do?

options.text: Create a Cloud Function that is triggered by a create type event in Firestore,
Create an email-sending application hosted on Compute Engine that is invoked by an HTTP request.
Create an email notification channel, and set up an alerting policy that is based on log metrics from a create type event.
Use Pub/Sub to send an email when the orders/ API returns an HTTP response of 200 OK.

questions.explanation:
A serverless Cloud Function can be triggered when a Firestore document is created and can run custom email-composition and sending logic. This event-driven approach avoids deploying and operating a Compute Engine-hosted application. Google Cloud documents Firestore document-created events as supported function triggers.

**Learn more:** [Create triggers from Firestore events](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/triggering/firestore-triggers)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are a lead developer at an organization that recently integrated several Google Cloud services. The services reside in Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) environments secured by VPC Service Controls and Private Service Connect endpoints. Developers throughout the organization use different operating systems, development frameworks, and integrated development environments (IDEs). You need to recommend a developer environment that ensures consistency in the development process and improves the overall developer experience. You want this solution to:  
  
- Enforce consistent security controls.  
- Access Google Cloud resources and applications within the VPC.  
- Permit installation of custom tools and utilities on the development environments.  
  
What solution should you recommend?

options.text: Use Cloud Workstations, and allow developers to create their own custom images.
Use Cloud Workstations with preconfigured base images. For custom tools and utilities, use custom images that are rebuilt weekly.
Use the Cloud Code extension with the IDEs that are used across the organization. Configure Cloud VPN to enable VPC access.
Use the Cloud Code extension with the IDEs that are used across the organization. Use Identity-Aware Proxy to enable access to the services in the VPC.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Workstations supplies centrally managed workstation configurations and container images, enabling a consistent, controlled development environment regardless of developers’ local operating systems or IDE preferences. It supports private workstation clusters connected to VPC networks with Private Service Connect and can be used with VPC Service Controls. Platform teams can provide custom container images with required tools and utilities; rebuilding those images regularly incorporates current base-image updates and security patches while preserving centrally enforced controls.

**Learn more:** [Cloud Workstations architecture](https://docs.cloud.google.com/workstations/docs/architecture) · [Configure VPC Service Controls and private clusters](https://docs.cloud.google.com/workstations/docs/configure-vpc-service-controls-private-clusters)

What should you do?
