questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are developing a mobile application that will store hierarchical data structures in a database. The application will let users working offline synchronize changes once they are online again. A backend service will enrich the database data by using a service account. The application is expected to be highly popular and must scale seamlessly and securely. Which database and IAM role should you use?

options.text: Use Cloud SQL, and assign the roles/cloudsql.editor role to the service account.
Use Bigtable, and assign the roles/bigtable.viewer role to the service account.
Use Firestore in Native mode and assign the roles/datastore.user role to the service account.
Use Firestore in Datastore mode and assign the roles/datastore.viewer role to the service account.

questions.explanation:
Firestore in Native mode supports hierarchical document data through collections and subcollections, mobile offline persistence that synchronizes local changes after reconnection, and automatic scaling. The `roles/datastore.user` role grants read/write access to Firestore data and is intended for application developers and service accounts, allowing the backend service to enrich stored data.

**Learn more:** [Choose between Firestore Native mode and Datastore mode](https://docs.cloud.google.com/datastore/docs/firestore-or-datastore) · [Security for Firestore server client libraries](https://docs.cloud.google.com/firestore/native/docs/security/iam?hl=en)

questions.domain: Deploying applications
questions.question:
You plan to deploy your application in a Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) cluster. The application can scale horizontally, and every application instance requires a stable network identity and its own persistent disk.  
  
Which GKE object should you use?

options.text: Deployment
StatefulSet
ReplicaSet
ReplicaController

questions.explanation:
A StatefulSet manages stateful Pods with stable, unique network identities and stable persistent storage. It can create a distinct PersistentVolumeClaim for each replica, preserving the association between that replica’s identity and storage across rescheduling.\
\
**Learn more:** [Kubernetes StatefulSets](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/controllers/statefulset/)

questions.domain: Integrating applications with Google Cloud services
questions.question:
You plan to deploy your application in a Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) cluster. The application can scale horizontally, and every application instance requires a stable network identity and its own persistent disk.  
  
Which GKE object should you use?

options.text: Store and retrieve the file contents using Compute Engine instance metadata.
Output the file contents to a file in /workspace. Read from the same /workspace file in the subsequent build step.
Use gsutil to output the file contents to a Cloud Storage object. Read from the same object in the subsequent build step.
Add a build argument that runs an HTTP POST via curl to a separate web server to persist the value in one builder. Use an HTTP GET via curl from the subsequent build step to read the value.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Build automatically mounts the `/workspace` volume in every build step. Files written to that location persist for the duration of the build and are available to subsequent build steps.

**Learn more:** [Passing data between build steps | Cloud Build](https://docs.cloud.google.com/build/docs/configuring-builds/pass-data-between-steps)

questions.domain: Integrating applications with Google Cloud services
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your team builds services that run on Google Kubernetes Engine. You need to standardize their log data by using Google-recommended practices and make that data more useful with the fewest steps. What should you do? (Choose two.)

options.text: Create aggregated exports on application logs to BigQuery to facilitate log analytics.
Create aggregated exports on application logs to Cloud Storage to facilitate log analytics.
Write log output to standard output (stdout) as single-line JSON to be ingested into Cloud Logging as structured logs.
Mandate the use of the Logging API in the application code to write structured logs to Cloud Logging.
Mandate the use of the Pub/Sub API to write structured data to Pub/Sub and create a Dataflow streaming pipeline to normalize logs and write them to BigQuery for analytics.

questions.explanation:
The GKE-integrated logging agent converts single-line JSON written to stdout or stderr into structured log entries in Cloud Logging, avoiding application-level Logging API integration. An aggregated sink can centralize matching logs and route them to BigQuery for analysis while retaining their structure; BigQuery is the appropriate destination for analytical queries.

**Learn more:** [About GKE logs](https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/about-logs) · [Aggregated sinks overview](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/export/aggregated_sinks_overview)

questions.domain: Deploying applications
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company is preparing a global event and needs to configure an event-registration portal. You have chosen to deploy the registration service using Cloud Run. The marketing team does not want to promote the Cloud Run service URL; instead, they want the registration portal accessible through a personalized hostname or path in the custom-domain URL pattern, for example, `.example.com`.  
  
How should you configure access to the service while following Google-recommended practices?

options.text: Configure Cloud Armor to block traffic on the Cloud Run service URL and allow reroutes from only the custom domain URL pattern.
Set up an HAProxy on Compute Engine, and add routing rules for a custom domain to the Cloud Run service URL.
Add a global external Application Load Balancer in front of the service, and configure a DNS record that points to the load balancer’s IP address.
Create a CNAME record that points to the Cloud Run service URL.

questions.explanation:
A global external Application Load Balancer is the recommended way to expose a Cloud Run service through a custom domain. Configure the custom domain at the load balancer and point its DNS record to the load balancer’s IP address; the load balancer can route hostname- or path-based traffic to the Cloud Run backend.

**Learn more:** [Mapping custom domains | Cloud Run](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/mapping-custom-domains) · [Set up a global external Application Load Balancer with Cloud Run](https://docs.cloud.google.com/load-balancing/docs/https/setup-global-ext-https-serverless)

questions.domain: Designing scalable, available, and reliable cloud-native applications
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your ecommerce application receives external requests and forwards them to third-party API services for credit card processing, shipping, and inventory management, as shown in the diagram.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783709186717-pu3thm4f.png)  
  
Customers report that the application runs slowly at unpredictable times. The application does not report any metrics. You need to identify the cause of the inconsistent performance. What should you do?

options.text: Install the OpenTelemetry library for your respective language, and instrument your application.
Install the Ops Agent inside your container and configure it to gather application metrics.
Modify your application to read and forward the X-Cloud-Trace-Context header when it calls the downstream services.
Enable Managed Service for Prometheus on the Google Kubernetes Engine cluster to gather application metrics.

questions.explanation:
Application instrumentation with OpenTelemetry collects application-level metrics and distributed traces, including latency for outbound calls to downstream services. That telemetry makes it possible to isolate whether intermittent slowness originates in the application or a particular third-party dependency. Google Cloud recommends OpenTelemetry for application instrumentation and notes that distributed traces show how multiple services interact while processing requests.

**Learn more:** [Instrumentation and observability](https://docs.cloud.google.com/stackdriver/docs/instrumentation/overview)

questions.domain: Building and testing applications
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are planning to run a load test for your Cloud Run service with JMeter. You need to coordinate the steps and services needed for effective load testing and analysis, following Google-recommended practices. What should you do?

options.text: Install JMeter on your local machine, create a log sink to BigQuery, and use Looker to analyze the results.
Set up a Compute Engine instance, install JMeter on the instance, create a log sink to a Cloud Storage bucket, and use Looker Studio to analyze the results.
Set up a Compute Engine instance, install JMeter on the instance, create a log sink to a Cloud Storage bucket, and use Looker to analyze the results.
Set up a Compute Engine instance, install JMeter on the instance, create a log sink to BigQuery, and use Looker Studio to analyze the results.

questions.explanation:
A Compute Engine VM provides a suitable environment for the JMeter test harness. Cloud Run guidance recommends exporting logs to BigQuery for detailed load-test analysis, and Looker Studio can connect to BigQuery to create visualizations and reports.

**Learn more:** [Cloud Run load testing best practices](https://cloud.google.com/run/docs/about-load-testing) · [Analyze data with Looker Studio](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/bi-engine-looker-studio)

questions.domain: Integrating applications with Google Cloud services
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A Python job run by your team reads millions of customer-record files stored in a Cloud Storage bucket. To meet regulatory requirements, customer data must be deleted immediately after the job finishes. You want to minimize the time needed to complete this task. What should you do?

options.text: Add a final step in the job that deletes all the objects in the bucket in bulk by using batch requests to the Cloud Storage API.
Configure Object Lifecycle Management on the Cloud Storage bucket that deletes all the objects in the bucket at the end of the job execution.
Remove the bucket from the Google Cloud console when the job is completed
Use the gcloud CLI to execute the gcloud storage rm --recursive gs://BUCKET_NAME/ command.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Storage JSON API batch requests combine up to 100 individual deletion calls into one HTTP request, reducing connection overhead when deleting many objects. A cleanup step at the end of the job therefore initiates deletion directly at job completion. Object Lifecycle Management is asynchronous and can lag after its conditions are met, so it cannot ensure deletion at that exact time.

**Learn more:** [Delete objects | Cloud Storage](https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/deleting-objects) · [Sending batch requests | Cloud Storage](https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/batch)

questions.question:
Your App Engine Standard configuration is:  
  
```yaml  
service: production  
instance_class: B1  
```  
  
You need to limit the application to 5 instances. Which configuration snippet should you include?

options.text: manual_scaling: instances: 5 min_pending_latency: 30ms
manual_scaling: max_instances: 5 idle_timeout: 10m
basic_scaling: instances: 5 min_pending_latency: 30ms
basic_scaling: max_instances: 5 idle_timeout: 10m

questions.explanation:
For App Engine Standard services using B1 or higher instance classes, `basic_scaling` supports the required `max_instances` setting, which sets the maximum number of instances App Engine can create for that service version. `idle_timeout` is an optional valid setting under `basic_scaling`.\
\
**Learn more:** [App Engine app.yaml reference](https://cloud.google.com/appengine/docs/standard/reference/app-yaml)

questions.question:
Your App Engine Standard configuration is:  
  
```yaml  
service: production  
instance_class: B1  
```  
  
You need to limit the application to 5 instances. Which configuration snippet should you include?

options.text: Deploy Zonal clusters
Deploy Regional clusters
Deploy Multi-Zone clusters
Deploy GKE on-premises clusters

questions.explanation:
Regional GKE clusters replicate the control plane across multiple zones within a region, so a single-zone failure does not take down the Kubernetes API. They also distribute worker nodes across multiple zones by default, improving workload availability when sufficient replicas and capacity are configured.

**Learn more:** [Regional clusters | Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE)](https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/regional-clusters) · [About cluster configuration choices | Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE)](https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/configuration-overview)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are creating a Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) cluster and execute this command:  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783706114248-9ozb6vpc.jpg)  
  
The command fails with this error:  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783706116646-yb2lklta.jpg)  
  
You want to fix the issue. What should you do?

options.text: Request additional GKE quota in the GCP Console.
Request additional Compute Engine quota in the GCP Console.
Open a support case to request additional GKE quota.
Decouple services in the cluster, and rewrite new clusters to function with fewer cores.

questions.explanation:
GKE cluster nodes run as Compute Engine VM instances, and the reported `CPUS` limit is a regional Compute Engine CPU quota. The requested 200 vCPUs exceed the 24 vCPUs available, so the project needs a Compute Engine CPU quota increase for that region through the Google Cloud console.

**Learn more:** [Compute Engine allocation quotas](https://docs.cloud.google.com/compute/resource-usage)

questions.domain: Integrating applications with Google Cloud services

options.text: Use HTTP signed URLs to securely provide access to the required resources.
Use the instance's service account Application Default Credentials to authenticate to the required resources.
Generate a P12 file from the GCP Console after the instance is deployed, and copy the credentials to the host instance before starting the application.
Commit the credential JSON file into your application's source repository, and have your CI/CD process package it with the software that is deployed to the instance.

questions.explanation:
For production workloads on Compute Engine, attach a least-privileged service account to the VM and use Application Default Credentials. ADC retrieves short-lived credentials for the attached service account through the metadata server, so no long-lived P12 or JSON service-account key must be copied to the instance or included in source and deployment artifacts.

**Learn more:** [How Application Default Credentials works](https://cloud.google.com/docs/authentication/application-default-credentials) · [Authenticate workloads to Google Cloud APIs using service accounts](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/access/authenticate-workloads)

Your team is developing an application for a financial institution. The application's frontend runs on Compute Engine, and its data is stored in Cloud SQL and a single Cloud Storage bucket. The application will collect data containing PII, which will be stored in the Cloud SQL database and the Cloud Storage bucket. You need to protect the PII data. What should you do?

options.text: 1. Create the relevant firewall rules to allow only the frontend to communicate with the Cloud SQL database2. Using IAM, allow only the frontend service account to access the Cloud Storage bucket
1. Create the relevant firewall rules to allow only the frontend to communicate with the Cloud SQL database2. Enable private access to allow the frontend to access the Cloud Storage bucket privately
1. Configure a private IP address for Cloud SQL2. Use VPC-SC to create a service perimeter3. Add the Cloud SQL database and the Cloud Storage bucket to the same service perimeter
1. Configure a private IP address for Cloud SQL2. Use VPC-SC to create a service perimeter3. Add the Cloud SQL database and the Cloud Storage bucket to different service perimeters

questions.explanation:
A private IP for Cloud SQL lets VPC resources communicate with the database through private connectivity rather than an external IP path. VPC Service Controls creates a security perimeter that helps mitigate data exfiltration for protected services, including Cloud SQL and Cloud Storage. Keeping the database and bucket in the same perimeter preserves the application's necessary access to both protected PII stores while constraining access outside that boundary.

**Learn more:** [Learn about using private IP | Cloud SQL](https://cloud.google.com/sql/docs/mysql/private-ip) · [Configure VPC Service Controls | Cloud SQL](https://cloud.google.com/sql/docs/sqlserver/admin-api/configure-service-controls)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are designing a schema for a Cloud Spanner customer database. You need to store an array field of phone numbers in a customer table, while also allowing users to search for customers by phone number.  
  
How should this schema be designed?

options.text: Create a table named Customers. Add an Array field in a table that will hold phone numbers for the customer.
Create a table named Customers. Create a table named Phones. Add a CustomerId field in the Phones table to find the CustomerId from a phone number.
Create a table named Customers. Add an Array field in a table that will hold phone numbers for the customer. Create a secondary index on the Array field.
Create a table named Customers as a parent table. Create a table named Phones, and interleave this table into the Customer table. Create an index on the phone number field in the Phones table.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Spanner ARRAY columns cannot be index key columns, and arrays are not intended for access to individual elements. Storing each phone number as a scalar value in a Phones child table allows a secondary index on that value for customer lookups. Interleaving the child table under Customers is an appropriate parent-child data model that colocates each customer’s phone records with the customer row.

**Learn more:** [Schemas overview | Spanner](https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/schema-and-data-model) · [GoogleSQL data definition language | Spanner](https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/reference/standard-sql/data-definition-language)

questions.domain: Integrating applications with Google Cloud services
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are developing a new application deployed on Cloud Run that uses Cloud Functions. Whenever new features are introduced, additional Cloud Functions and Cloud Run services are deployed. You use environment variables to track the services and allow interservice communication, but maintaining those environment variables has become challenging. You want to implement dynamic discovery in a scalable manner. What should you do?

options.text: Configure your microservices to use the Cloud Run Admin and Cloud Functions APIs to query for deployed Cloud Run services and Cloud Functions in the Google Cloud project.
Create a Service Directory namespace. Use API calls to register the services during deployment, and query during runtime.
Rename the Cloud Functions and Cloud Run services endpoint is using a well-documented naming convention.
Deploy Hashicorp Consul on a single Compute Engine instance. Register the services with Consul during deployment, and query during runtime.

questions.explanation:
Service Directory is a managed platform for publishing, discovering, and connecting services. Services and their endpoints can be registered during deployment in a namespace, and workloads can resolve the registered service at runtime, removing the need to manually maintain environment variables.

**Learn more:** [Service Directory API](https://docs.cloud.google.com/service-directory/docs/reference/rest)
